rationale: The four views consistently show a low, horizontally layered composition with displaced parallel bars, so the candidate is not coherent in only one view. However, the primary bars are difficult to distinguish from the podium and numerous thin projections. The massing reads more as a collection of overlapping platforms than as a strong twin-bar composition. A shallow central separation suggests a void, but it is not large or legible enough to read as a meaningful public courtyard or undercut. The stepped platform language resonates with the cited OMA precedents, though the diagram lacks their stronger sectional hierarchy and dominant anchor.
warnings: The primary mass is visually weak and nearly merges with the podium.
Multiple thin surface pieces and offsets dilute the dominant gesture.
Several layers appear to overlap or collide rather than register as clearly separated solids.
The central open space is too shallow and fragmented to read as a strong public void.
